developer_comments: A goal broken into steps, drawn as a map; every step is taught by a full subject. Product term, capitalised in English; one fixed translation everywhere. (catalog: top.curricula)
One stop on a Roadmap; each step is a subject. Called “station” on the map (same translation). (catalog: sh.nextStep)
Synonym of “step” on the Roadmap map and its legend; translate exactly like step. (catalog: sh.signRule)
What a Roadmap leads to (typed by the learner), drawn as the treasure on the map. Also the daily XP goal. (catalog: top.curriculaTitle)
The Roadmap’s goal on the map; on Progress also the medals the learner found (“Treasures you found”). (catalog: sh.treasures)
The drawing of a Roadmap (as opposed to the list view). (catalog: sh.viewMap)
The outline of a Roadmap step (its chapters) that the learner can look over before the step is prepared. Not the Claude subscription plan. (catalog: sh.signReview)
Plan a Roadmap step again (e.g. to match a subject attached to it). (catalog: sh.signReplan)
A step is “prepared” when its subject has been generated (by the AI or another member); “being prepared” while that runs. (catalog: sh.signBusy)
Put a subject the learner already has on a Roadmap step, so that it teaches that step. (catalog: sh.rmAttach)
Master a step: read all its sections and solve at least 80% of its exercises (or pass the “I already know this” test). (catalog: sh.stationDone)
State of a Roadmap step the learner can study now. (catalog: sh.signOpen)
State of a Roadmap step whose earlier steps are not mastered yet. (catalog: sh.signLocked)
Where the subjects that are not a step of any Roadmap stay. Product term. (catalog: sh.shelf)
A study pack about one topic (chapters, sections, exercises, flashcards, tutor), made by the learner, Claude or others. Not a language course. (catalog: sh.allSubjects)
A subject as a file to import or create (.zip/.json). (catalog: pick.import)
What the learner’s sources become when Claude creates a subject from them. (catalog: pick.none)
An exported subject with its source files (.zip), or a subject file to import. (catalog: sh.exportPackage)
A part of a subject; it has sections, exercises, traps and a boss. (catalog: home.chapters)
A reading unit of a chapter (theory), ending with a quick check. (catalog: sh.nextSection)
The reading part of a subject (as opposed to practice). (catalog: sh.theory)
A question or task to solve (multiple choice, free answer, …). (catalog: sh.exercisesWord)
Doing exercises (tab of a chapter, progress bar label). (catalog: sh.practice)
To do exercises on something. (catalog: sh.chooseRound)
A file (PDF, notes, link) a subject or step was made from. (catalog: sh.sources)
Cards for recall practice with spaced repetition. Product term. (catalog: home.cards)
One flashcard. (catalog: sh.viewCards)
Reviewing at growing intervals. (catalog: home.cardsSub)
Today’s review of everything due (flashcards and debugging checklists of all subjects); also the reviews of a language course. (catalog: sh.review)
Waiting to be reviewed today (“5 due”). (catalog: home.due)
Drills that make the learner memorise the “ask yourself” debugging checklists of a subject. (catalog: home.drills)
A debugging checklist: the questions to ask yourself when something goes wrong. (catalog: sh.reviewTip)
A detail easy to confuse or a classic mistake of a chapter (pitfall). “Traps” is a chapter tab. (catalog: ch.traps)
60 seconds of quick true/false questions about traps. Product term. (catalog: home.lightning)
All the exercises the learner got wrong; each leaves when answered right. Product term. (catalog: home.mistakes)
A wrong answer. (catalog: sh.gymNone)
Random exercises from everything read. (catalog: home.mixed)
The few questions at the end of a section. (catalog: sh.quickCheck)
The final test of a chapter, with 3 lives (game metaphor). (catalog: sh.boss)
One of the 3 chances in a boss fight (“3 lives”). (catalog: sh.bossSub)
A short series of exercises (“A round of 10”). (catalog: sh.round10)
15 minutes of concentrated study, then a short break. (catalog: sh.focusSprint)
Setting: the theory appears chunk by chunk. (catalog: sh.chunk)
The number of consecutive days with study. (catalog: sh.streakStart)
Experience points earned by studying. Keep “XP” unless your language has a firmly established abbreviation. (catalog: sh.xpWeek)
The learner’s level, earned with XP; each level opens a new place of the character’s world. (catalog: sh.level)
The XP the learner wants to earn per day. (catalog: sh.goalTitle)
The items (stars, shells … depending on the character) the learner collects, one per completed chapter. (catalog: sh.gameModeSub)
The character’s world that themes the app (map landscape, places opened by levels). (catalog: sh.xpTotal)
The character’s animated reaction to what the learner did. (catalog: sh.gameModeSub)
The game layer of the app (“How much game”: reactions, collection, treasures). (catalog: sh.gameMode)
Game setting: big reactions now and then and at milestones. (catalog: sh.gamePlayful)
Game setting: reactions only at milestones. (catalog: sh.gameCalm)
The AI that teaches inside the app, embodied by the learner’s character. In shell messages the character’s name fills {tutor}. (catalog: top.tutor)
The figure the learner chooses (a pet, a fairy-tale figure, a serious character); it is also the tutor and themes the app. (catalog: sh.character)
The character seen as the companion of the learner’s journey. (catalog: sh.companion)
Tutor mode: the tutor guides by asking questions. (catalog: sh.chSocratic)
Tutor mode: the tutor explains in depth, no quiz. (catalog: sh.modeExplain)
Tutor mode: quick questions, one at a time. (catalog: sh.modeQuiz)
Tutor mode: a mock job interview on the subject. (catalog: sh.modeInterview)
Tutor mode: a broken case (a failing system, a patient …) for the learner to diagnose. (catalog: sh.modeDebug)
Tutor mode on an exercise: a nudge, never the answer. (catalog: sh.modeHint)
A chat with the tutor, kept in the conversation history. (catalog: sh.activity)
Tab: the daily home page. (catalog: sh.today)
Tab: Roadmaps and subjects (fields of knowledge, as opposed to languages). (catalog: sh.knowledge)
Tab: the language courses. (catalog: sh.languages)
Tab: discover and add things (new Roadmaps, imports, what others share, Claude). (catalog: sh.discover)
Tab: level, XP, streak, collection, treasures. (catalog: sh.progress)
Tab: the learner’s own account (profile, settings, data). Very short. (catalog: sh.me)
The catalogue of public subjects other people share. (catalog: top.explore)
Shares, invitations and updates, collected in the bell. (catalog: sh.notifications)
The 🔔 button that holds the notifications. (catalog: sh.decideLater)
Settings of the app, a Roadmap or a course. (catalog: sh.rmSettings)
A course of the language module (one or several languages learned together). (catalog: sh.langNew)
Short for language course (in menus: “Course settings”, “Choose another course”). (catalog: sh.langSettings)
A lesson of a language course (or the lessons where the tutor teaches). (catalog: sh.onbWhoSub)
Today’s study session of a language course. (catalog: sh.langSession)
A word of the learned language (“words met”). (catalog: sh.langWords)
A person using the app (local on this device, or a cloud account). (catalog: sh.profile)
A profile stored only on this device. (catalog: pick.local)
An online account that syncs progress across devices. (catalog: sh.notesNeedCloud)
Synchronisation of data between devices. (catalog: sh.data)
A copy of all data that can be restored. (catalog: sh.backup)
Bringing data back from a backup. (catalog: sh.dataSub)
Share a subject or a Roadmap with people or make it public. (catalog: sh.share)
Visible to every learner (public subjects and Roadmaps). (catalog: sh.noPublicSubjects)
Only for the learner (a subject they made and did not share). (catalog: sh.privateSubj)
Become a member of a shared or public Roadmap (own progress, shared prepared steps). (catalog: sh.rmJoin)
A person who joined a shared Roadmap. (catalog: sh.signShared)
Ask someone to join a Roadmap. (catalog: sh.invitesYou)
A subject the learner hid from the lists (not deleted). (catalog: sh.hiddenN)
Bring a subject or Roadmap file into the app. (catalog: sh.importFile)
Download a conversation, subject or Roadmap as a file. (catalog: sh.exportMd)
Artificial intelligence (the tutor, generated questions, prepared steps). Use the usual abbreviation of your language. (catalog: sh.rmSettingsSub)
Anthropic’s AI. A product name: never translated or transliterated (Greek: neuter, “το Claude”). (catalog: pick.create)
The learner’s own Claude app (claude.ai) connected to noema-lite, which prepares subjects and Roadmaps with their Claude plan. (catalog: sh.claudeApp)
A pay-per-use developer key (Claude or Gemini) entered in the app. (catalog: sh.claudeKey)
Google’s AI used by the tutor with the learner’s key. A product name: never translated. (catalog: home.tutorSub)
The product name (also “Noema”). Never translated; keep the lower case and the hyphen. (catalog: sh.joinNeedsCloud)
